props.title: Demons
props.initialSlug: Demonic evil spreads through a cursed movie theater

sections.content: **Demons** (1985) marks a gloriously gory high point in Italian horror, produced by Dario Argento and directed by Lamberto Bava. The film's premise - demons possessing moviegoers inside a theater - creates a meta-horror masterpiece that influenced films like **Popcorn** (1991) and **Midnight Movie** (2008). The practical effects by Sergio Stivaletti set a new standard for 1980s creature features, rivaling the work in John Carpenter's **The Thing** (1982) and **The Howling** (1981). The film's pulsing heavy metal soundtrack and neon-drenched cinematography perfectly capture the excess of 1980s Euro-horror.

sections.content: The success of **Demons** sparked a wave of Italian meta-horror films. Michele Soavi's **Stage Fright** (1987) and **The Church** (1989) built on its foundation of blending supernatural threats with confined spaces. The film's influence extends to modern meta-horror like **Scary Movie** (2000) and **The Cabin in the Woods** (2012), which similarly play with horror conventions while delivering genuine scares.

The film's creature designs deserve special attention, showcasing the pinnacle of Italian practical effects work. The transformation sequences rival those in David Cronenberg's **The Fly** (1986) and **Videodrome** (1983), emphasizing body horror and grotesque physical mutations. This approach influenced later films like **From Dusk Till Dawn** (1996) and **Night of the Demons** (1988). SUBHEAD: Italian Horror's Golden Age

movies.title: Cemetery Man
movies.slug: Rupert Everett stars in this surreal Italian zombie film that blends horror and dark comedy

sections.content: **Demons** represents the commercial peak of Italian horror's golden age, alongside Lucio Fulci's **The Beyond** (1981) and **City of the Living Dead** (1980). The film's success allowed Dario Argento to continue producing ambitious horror projects through the 1980s, including **Opera** (1987) and **Phenomena** (1985), maintaining Italy's position as a horror powerhouse.
